mechanism: Manufacturers' new-orders growth reflects business demand for goods and forward production plans; strong rising orders are risk-on for equities and slowing orders are an early demand-softening signal. Exposure is scaled toward SPY when new-orders growth is firm.
key_finding: Best search-phase rule uses yoy at L12 with OOS Sharpe 1.56 versus buy-and-hold 0.96.
caveats: Even a leading indicator selected at a long lead can be a search artifact — check adjacent-lead durability.
The strategy is search-selected and needs fresh holdout validation.
The 2020-21 COVID collapse/rebound is an extreme in-window outlier that can dominate the fit.
New-orders figures are nominal and revised in later Census M3 releases.
narrative_summary: Manufacturers' new-orders growth is tested as a procyclical / leading factory-demand overlay for SPY, not as a clean leading indicator.

known_stress_episodes.note: New orders fell with the tech capex bust.
